author: kingpanther13
releaseNotes:
v4.7.0 - 2026-10-11
- docs: note mcp-proxy 0.13.0 fixes the startup crash, keep mcp-remote for Claude Desktop (#528)
  - Claude Desktop docs: `mcp-proxy` 0.13.0 starts again without an SDK pin, but slow writes still need `mcp-remote` with `--protocol auto`.
- feat: deliver one inlined parent app through HPM instead of a library bundle (#525)
  - Installs and updates through Hubitat Package Manager are now a single app save instead of a bundle plus an app save, so an update no longer fails with "Read timed out" and then retries; on a C-8 an update takes about four minutes instead of nine.
  - The Groovy libraries are no longer installed separately. After this update the old `mcp` libraries and the `mcp_libraries` bundle remain under Libraries Code and Bundles as unused code; they can be deleted by hand at any time.
  - Manual (non-HPM) installs now use the release build URLs on the `bundle-artifacts` branch (see README).
  - If you upgrade from 4.6.0 or earlier with the Developer-Mode `hub_update_package` tool, do that one upgrade through HPM instead: the 4.6.0 tool expects a library bundle and refuses the new layout. From this version on it deploys any ref again.
  - Updating app code from a URL (`importUrl`) no longer writes a pre-update source backup to File Manager: the previous version lives wherever that URL is published. Updates from inline source or a File Manager file still back up first unless you pass `backup: false`.
  - A Developer-Mode self-update now returns as soon as the hub has accepted the save (`status: "saving"`) and `hub_get_info` reports when the new version is compiled, instead of the request timing out after five minutes.
  - Deleting the leftover `mcp` libraries after the upgrade is recommended: each one adds about half a second to the Libraries Code page and to `hub_list_libraries` on a C-8 (README explains).
